newsitem.title: USA: US Sen. Lott--budget tax-cut issue can be resolved.
newsitem.headline: US Sen. Lott--budget tax-cut issue can be resolved.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Wednesday he expects differences with the White House over tax cut proposals can be resolved as they negotiate a five-year balanced budget.

Speaking to reporters, the Mississippi Republican said, "We still have a little more adjustment we need to make on the tax side. They still want to get more tax increases than we think are achievable. We still would like to have more net tax cuts than have been agreed to. But it's close," he said.

"That ought to be a problem we can resolve," Lott said of the tax cut issues. Republicans have said they want a $100 billion net tax cut over five years while the administration has asked for a gross tax cut of $98 billion offset by $76 in tax hikes.
